study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective observational cohort study
outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (NICU admission, RDS, TTN, hypoglycemia, mechanical ventilation, sepsis, length of stay ≥5 days, neonatal death)
Composite maternal morbidity (uterine rupture, blood transfusion, general anesthesia, cesarean hysterectomy, venous thromboembolism, maternal sepsis, ICU admission, surgical complications)
cohort: 436 women with a prior classical cesarean delivery undergoing repeat cesarean delivery
finding: In women undergoing repeat cesarean delivery after a prior classical cesarean delivery, delivery at 37 weeks gestation was associated with a decrease in composite neonatal morbidity compared to delivery at 36 weeks gestation.
